correctness.rationale: The Poincaré first return map near any regular periodic orbit in dimension two is locally invertible; its square is increasing, hence every sufficiently nearby initial state has at least one complete semiorbit trapped within any prescribed orbit tube. Observable speed zero along a candidate periodic orbit is necessary, so two-sided finite slow-region exits are impossible. In the complete three-dimensional rational oscillator, the exact radial first integral and z(t)=epsilon exp(-t) prove monotone speed from -infinity to +infinity, both logarithmic delay constants and reachability for every point of the unit-circle saddle orbit. The included verification program reconstructs critical identities.

value.rationale: The two-sided reachable-transient-center notion is distinct from repulsion or slow transient behavior in one time direction. A universal obstruction for periodic nonequilibrium states below dimension three, with no hyperbolicity assumptions, determines the smallest dimension that supports this type of recurrent organizing center. The constructed three-dimensional witness is globally complete and supplies exact forward/backward delay constants, showing the bound is sharp.
